title: Ribbed cowl
subtitle: A 2x2 rib tube worked in the round with a stretchy fit.
excerpt: A cowl knitted in the round in 2x2 rib on 5 mm needles with worsted-weight yarn, finishing at 55 cm circumference relaxed and 24 cm tall. The rib pattern is fully reversible and stretches generously around the neck. Both the cast-on and bind-off use the Italian tubular method for a seamless, polished edge on each opening.
sourceNotes: Ribbed neckwarmers worked in the round appear throughout Weldon's Practical Knitter (1880s-1900s), Internet Archive. The 2x2 rib is documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), citations only.

glossaryTerms.definition: A rib pattern that alternates two knit stitches with two purl stitches across every row or round, producing a stretchy, textured fabric that is nearly identical on both sides.
Knitting a small circumference in the round on one long circular needle by pulling a loop of cable through the work at the halfway point.
A cast-on forming a neat elastic edge by using the tail and working yarn over two fingers simultaneously.

content.text: This is a cowl knitted in the round in
2x2 rib

on 5 mm needles with worsted-weight yarn, finishing at 55 cm circumference relaxed and 24 cm tall. The rib is fully reversible and stretches generously, so the cowl fits a range of neck sizes without a choice of sizes. The construction is in-the-round with no seam.
In-the-round construction was chosen because a full rib tube has no reason to have a seam: the rib pattern is the same on both faces and continues seamlessly around the circumference. The
magic loop
method on an 80 cm circular needle handles 100 stitches comfortably. The finished cowl needs about 180 m (approximately 100 g) of worsted-weight yarn.
What you need

items.name: Worsted-weight wool or wool-blend yarn
items.substitutions: Any worsted-weight yarn. Wool gives the best elasticity for rib.

content.text: Gauge

18 sts x 24 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch in the round on 5 mm needles. The 2x2 rib relaxed is approximately 14 sts per 10 cm because the rib compresses sideways. Measure the swatch relaxed without stretching. One stitch per 10 cm off gauge shifts the finished circumference (relaxed) by approximately 4 cm at this stitch count. Round gauge drift across the 53 body rounds changes the finished height by up to 5 cm.
Stitches used
K (knit): right needle from left to right through front of stitch, wrap yarn counterclockwise, draw loop through.
P (purl): right needle from right to left through front of stitch with yarn in front, wrap yarn, draw loop through to back.
Pattern
Cast on
Use the
long-tail cast-on

to place 100 stitches on the needle. The stitch count must be a multiple of 4 for 2x2 rib: 100 = 25 x 4. Before beginning, calculate the tail: tail_cm = (needle circumference mm x stitch count) / 10 + 15. For 5 mm needles (circumference approximately 15.7 mm) and 100 stitches: (15.7 x 100) / 10 + 15 = 157 + 15 = 172 cm. Leave a tail of at least 172 cm; wind it loosely.
Stitch count check-in: after the cast-on you should have 100 stitches on the needle. Join carefully to work in the round without twisting. Place a stitch marker.
Body
Every round: *K2, P2; repeat from * to end. (100 sts)
Work in 2x2 rib until the cowl measures 24 cm from the cast-on edge. At the halfway mark (approximately round 27 of 53 body rounds), count your stitches.
Stitch count check-in: at round 27 you should have 100 stitches on the needle.
Bind off

Stretchy bind-off in rib pattern: work each stitch in pattern and use the K2tog-tbl method, slipping the result back to the left needle before the next repeat. A standard bind-off leaves a narrower top opening than the body. The stretchy bind-off matches the rib elasticity.
Common faults

Rib alignment shifting after a missed round. If a round is half-worked and then restarted from the beginning, the K2 and P2 blocks can shift by one or two stitches. Use a stitch marker at the round start and confirm the K2 always lands on the same stitches each round.
Bound-off edge visibly narrower than cast-on edge. This is a standard-bind-off problem on rib. Always use the stretchy bind-off or bind off on a needle two sizes larger for rib.

Cowl looks shorter than expected before first wear. Rib compresses in the row dimension. Measure from the inside of the folded cowl, not the outside edge, for the most accurate height. The cowl relaxes and lengthens once worn.
Finishing

Weave in both tails at the cast-on join and bind-off edge. The ribbed cowl does not need blocking. If it has grown in height during knitting, pin gently to the stated dimensions and leave flat overnight.
Care
Handwash in cool water with wool wash. Lay flat over a round form to dry. The rib will spring back to its natural compressed width once dry.
What to try next
